symbols.def: Number of endogenous variables.

symbols.name: m
symbols.def: Number of observed environment slots.

symbols.name: c
symbols.def: Maximum number of arbitrarily replaced covariance slots.

symbols.name: E
symbols.def: Set of observed environment labels.

symbols.name: H
symbols.def: Unknown honest set with \(\lvert H\rvert=h\).

symbols.def: Cone of real symmetric positive-semidefinite \(p\times p\) matrices.

symbols.def: Cone of real symmetric positive-definite \(p\times p\) matrices.

symbols.def: Observed population covariance family \(\Sigma=(\Sigma_e:e\in E)\), with every observed or replaced slot chosen from the positive-definite covariance domain.

symbols.name: D
symbols.def: Structural demixing matrix in the equilibrium equation.

symbols.name: H2
symbols.def: Fitted slot set of the second competing BACKSHIFT explanation, with \(\lvert H_2\rvert\ge h\).

symbols.name: D2

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: Connectivity matrix \(B=I_p-D\).
symbols.role: Causal connectivity target reported by BACKSHIFT.

symbols.name: CP
symbols.def: Maximum absolute product along a directed simple cycle of length at least two.

symbols.name: Dcal
symbols.def: Matrix set satisfying the BACKSHIFT unit-diagonal and cycle-product normalization defined in \(\text{def:admissible-matrices}\).

symbols.name: Omega
symbols.def: Invariant disturbance covariance, permitted to be nondiagonal.

symbols.name: s

symbols.def: Shift levels \(s^{(1)}=(s^{(1)}_{ek}:e\in H_1,1\le k\le p)\) in the first competing explanation.

symbols.name: s2
symbols.def: Shift levels \(s^{(2)}=(s^{(2)}_{ek}:e\in H_2,1\le k\le p)\) in the second competing explanation.
symbols.role: Second explanation's shifts on the overlap.

symbols.name: L
symbols.space: \(\{L:L\text{ is an affine line in }\mathbb R^2\}\)
symbols.def: Generic affine line used to measure concentration of a pairwise shift cloud.

symbols.name: Mkl
symbols.def: Maximum affine-line occupancy \(M_{k\ell}=\max_L\#\{e\in H:(s_{ek},s_{e\ell})\in L\}\).

symbols.name: delta
symbols.def: Environment deletion distance \(\delta_H=\min_{1\le k<\ell\le p}(h-M_{k\ell})\).

symbols.name: Z
symbols.def: Proposal-specific prespecified support pattern for shift amplitudes.

symbols.name: a
symbols.def: Random positive amplitudes indexed by the honest environment and coordinate.

symbols.name: Mgen
symbols.def: Generic occupancy formula \(M_{k\ell}^{\mathrm{gen}}=\max\{n_{00}^{k\ell}+n_{10}^{k\ell},n_{00}^{k\ell}+n_{01}^{k\ell},n_{00}^{k\ell}+\mathbf 1\{n_{11}^{k\ell}>0\},\min(2,h)\}\).

symbols.name: Rc
symbols.def: Population \(c\)-replacement compatibility set defined in \(\text{def:compatible-set}\).
symbols.role: Recovery map for the structural target.

symbols.name: SubsetConsensus
symbols.def: Finite reduction of \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\) to exact feasibility-oracle queries over subsets of size \(h\), defined in \(\text{def:subset-consensus}\).
symbols.role: Definitional computational interface, not a supplied terminating solver.

symbols.name: gamma
symbols.def: Worst-overlap affine-minor separation, equal to zero when \(h-c<3\) and otherwise \(\gamma_H=\min_{k<\ell}\min_{S\subseteq H,\,|S|=h-c}\max_{e<f<g\in S}|\det[(1,s_{rk},s_{r\ell})_{r\in\{e,f,g\}}]|\).

symbols.def: Condition number \(\kappa_D=\|D\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|D^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\).

symbols.name: zeta

symbols.name: lambda
symbols.def: Positive-definiteness margin \(\lambda_H=\min\{\lambda_{\min}(\Omega),\min_{e\in H}\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_e)\}\).

symbols.name: Mbound
symbols.def: Operator-norm scale bound \(M_H=1+\|\Omega\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\max_{e\in H}\|\Sigma_e\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\max_{e\in H}\|\operatorname{diag}(s_e)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\).

symbols.name: n
symbols.def: Common within-environment sample-size index.
symbols.role: Asymptotic index for the inference layer.

symbols.name: alpha
symbols.def: Nominal noncoverage probability.

symbols.name: Calpha

symbols.def: Honest-slot simultaneous operator-norm radius \(r_{n,\alpha,H}=\max_{e\in H}\sup_{\Gamma\in\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}}\|\Gamma-\Sigma_e\|_{\mathrm{op}}\), with value \(+\infty\) allowed.

symbols.role: One-sided contraction criterion for the confidence union.

symbols.name: lambda0

novel.justification: Strict positivity is imposed only for the fixed-instance sharp converse and quantitative conditioning. Uniqueness and sufficiency hold on the published positive-semidefinite class; an ambiguity in this positive-definite subclass proves minimax sharpness over the larger class without asserting ambiguity at every singular boundary instance.

assumptions.condition: \(s_{ek}\ge0\) for every \(e\in H\) and \(1\le k\le p\).

standard.name: Population BACKSHIFT covariance equation, with the invariant-noise cone stated separately.

assumptions.condition: \(s_{ek}=Z_{ek}a_{ek}\) for every \(e\in H\) and \(1\le k\le p\).

novel.justification: The prespecified-support factorization is a proposal-specific restriction that conditions on an investigator-chosen sparse intervention design. It is realistic in multi-environment experiments whose intervention targets are fixed before continuously distributed positive doses are assigned.

assumptions.condition: The joint law of \((a_{ek}:e\in H,1\le k\le p,Z_{ek}=1)\) is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure on its positive orthant.

novel.justification: Joint absolute continuity conditional on a fixed sparse support pattern is a genericity condition for nonzero intervention strengths. It is satisfied when active intervention variances have a joint density on the positive orthant, including independently randomized positive strengths and correlated continuously distributed dose designs.

definitions.name: Mkl
definitions.construction: For \(1\le k<\ell\le p\), \(M_{k\ell}=\max_{L\subset\mathbb R^2\,\mathrm{affine\ line}}\#\{e\in H:(s_{ek},s_{e\ell})\in L\}\).

definitions.name: Rc
definitions.construction: For \(\Sigma\in(\mathbb S_{++}^{p})^{E}\), \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)=\{A\in\mathcal D:\exists K\subseteq E,\ |K|\ge h,\ \exists\Psi\in\mathbb S_{+}^p,\ \exists t_e\in[0,\infty)^p,\ \Sigma_e=A^{-1}(\Psi+\operatorname{diag}(t_e))A^{-\mathsf T}\ \forall e\in K\}\).

definitions.name: gamma
definitions.construction: Set \(\gamma_H=0\) when \(h-c<3\); otherwise set \(\gamma_H=\min_{1\le k<\ell\le p}\min_{S\subseteq H,\,|S|=h-c}\max_{e<f<g\in S}\left|\det\begin{pmatrix}1&s_{ek}&s_{e\ell}\\1&s_{fk}&s_{f\ell}\\1&s_{gk}&s_{g\ell}\end{pmatrix}\right|\).

definitions.name: SubsetConsensus
definitions.construction: Definitional implementation note: given a feasibility oracle that returns the full solution set for each queried semialgebraic system, query every \(K\subseteq E\) with \(|K|=h\) for all \(A\in\mathcal D\) satisfying \(\operatorname{offdiag}(A(\Sigma_e-\Sigma_f)A^{\mathsf T})=0\) for \(e,f\in K\) and admitting one \(\Psi\in\mathbb S_{+}^p\) with nonnegative diagonal shifts for the transformed raw covariances. Define \(\text{SubsetConsensus}(\Sigma,c)\) as the union of the oracle-returned solution sets. This enumeration makes exactly \(\binom{m}{h}\) oracle queries and, by expansion of \(\text{def:compatible-set}\), its returned union equals \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\); neither fact is a theorem contribution or a claim that an encoded terminating solver is supplied.

definitions.name: rRadius
definitions.construction: \(r_{n,\alpha,H}=\max_{e\in H}\sup_{\Gamma\in\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}}\|\Gamma-\Sigma_e\|_{\mathrm{op}}\in[0,+\infty]\), where the supremum and hence the maximum may equal \(+\infty\).

definitions.name: diamOp
definitions.construction: For every nonempty matrix set \(\mathcal A\), \(\operatorname{diam}_{\mathrm{op}}(\mathcal A)=\sup_{A_1,A_2\in\mathcal A}\|A_1-A_2\|_{\mathrm{op}}\in[0,+\infty]\).

definitions.name: outerOp
definitions.construction: For every nonempty matrix set \(\mathcal A\) and matrix \(D\), \(\operatorname{outer}_{\mathrm{op}}(\mathcal A,D)=\sup_{A_1\in\mathcal A}\|A_1-D\|_{\mathrm{op}}\in[0,+\infty]\).

definitions.name: Ualpha
definitions.construction: For each \(n\ge1\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), \(\mathcal U^{(n)}_{\alpha}=\bigcup\{\mathcal R_c(\Gamma):\Gamma_e\in\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\text{ for every }e\in E\}\). On the simultaneous honest-slot coverage event \(\{\Sigma_e\in\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\text{ for every }e\in H\}\), take \(\Gamma_e=\Sigma_e\) for \(e\in H\) and choose an arbitrary point of the nonempty region \(\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\) for each \(e\in E\setminus H\); then \(D\in\mathcal R_c(\Gamma)\subseteq\mathcal U^{(n)}_{\alpha}\). Thus simultaneous honest-slot coverage of probability at least \(1-\alpha\) yields \(\Pr\{D\in\mathcal U^{(n)}_{\alpha}\}\ge1-\alpha\). If every region is the singleton \(\{\Sigma_e\}\) and \(\delta_H>c\), the sharp replacement-radius theorem gives the unlabeled sanity conclusion \(\mathcal U^{(n)}_{\alpha}=\{D\}\).

definitions.name: CertificateInferenceHandle
definitions.construction: Start from the finite subset enumeration in \(\text{def:subset-consensus}\), represent noncollinearity without division by homogeneous \(3\times3\) affine minors, obtain operator-norm local perturbation control from the joint-diagonalization linearization indexed by \(\gamma_H,\kappa_D,\zeta_D,\lambda_H,M_H\), invert the indexed simultaneous covariance regions, and switch normalization charts only after forming chart-valid certificates.

statements.statement: Let the first explanation \(D^{(1)},H_1,s^{(1)}\) and the second explanation \(D^{(2)},H_2,s^{(2)}\) fit the same \(\Sigma\), each through a BACKSHIFT covariance equation satisfying the unit-diagonal and cycle-product normalization, with its own invariant positive-semidefinite nuisance, nonnegative shifts, and \(|H_r|\ge h=m-c\). Set \(J=H_1\cap H_2\). Then \(|J|\ge m-2c=h-c\). If, for every \(k<\ell\), the first explanation's cloud \(\{(s^{(1)}_{ek},s^{(1)}_{e\ell}):e\in J\}\) is not contained in an affine line, then \(D^{(1)}=D^{(2)}\).
statements.justification: This isolates the new robust step: competing explanations share only \(m-2c\) slots, on which ordinary congruence-diagonalizer uniqueness must be normalized causally.
statements.gap: RothenhauslerEtAl2015BackShift, Theorem 1, and KleinsteuberShen2013NUJDUniqueness, Theorem 1, treat a fixed complete diagonalizable family rather than the intersection of two adversarially selected families.
statements.consumer: The lemma supplies the sufficiency half of the exact replacement-radius theorem after two candidate honest sets lose different slots.
statements.proof_tex:
For \(r\in\{1,2\}\), let \(\Psi^{(r)}\in\mathbb S_+^p\) denote the invariant nuisance in the \(r\)-th fitted BACKSHIFT equation.  Thus, by the fitting hypotheses in the statement,
\[
D^{(r)}\Sigma_eD^{(r)\mathsf T}
 =\Psi^{(r)}+\operatorname{diag}(s^{(r)}_e),
 \qquad e\in H_r.
\]
First, inclusion--exclusion and \(|E|=m\), \(|H_r|\ge h=m-c\), give
\[
 |J|=|H_1\cap H_2|
 =|H_1|+|H_2|-|H_1\cup H_2|
 \ge 2h-m=m-2c=h-c.
\]

It remains to prove uniqueness.  Set \(Q=D^{(2)}(D^{(1)})^{-1}\).  The assumed noncollinearity implies that \(J\) is nonempty; fix \(e_0\in J\).  Subtracting the equation at \(e_0\) from the equation at \(e\in J\), and using the two displayed fits, yields
\[
 Q\operatorname{diag}(x_e)Q^{\mathsf T}
   =\operatorname{diag}(y_e),\qquad
 x_e=s^{(1)}_e-s^{(1)}_{e_0},\quad
 y_e=s^{(2)}_e-s^{(2)}_{e_0}.
\]
Let \(W=\operatorname{span}\{x_e:e\in J\}\subseteq\mathbb R^p\).  By linearity,
\[
 Q\operatorname{diag}(w)Q^{\mathsf T}\ \text{is diagonal for every }w\in W. \tag{1}
\]
For each \(k<\ell\), the coordinate projection of \(W\) onto coordinates \(k,\ell\) is all of \(\mathbb R^2\).  Indeed, if that projection had dimension at most one, some nonzero \((a,b)\in\mathbb R^2\) would satisfy
\[
 a(s^{(1)}_{ek}-s^{(1)}_{e_0k})
 +b(s^{(1)}_{e\ell}-s^{(1)}_{e_0\ell})=0
 \quad\text{for every }e\in J,
\]
placing the entire \(k,\ell\) cloud in one affine line, contrary to the hypothesis.

Put \(d_W=\dim(W)\).  Choose a basis \(w^1,\ldots,w^{d_W}\) of \(W\), and define its \(k\)-th coordinate profile by
\[
 u_k=(w^1_k,\ldots,w^{d_W}_k)^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{d_W}.
\]
The preceding projection assertion says that \(u_k,u_\ell\) are linearly independent whenever \(k\ne\ell\).  In particular, every \(u_k\) is nonzero.  Choose \(\beta\in\mathbb R^{d_W}\) outside the finitely many hyperplanes \(\{\beta:\beta^{\mathsf T}u_k=0\}\).  Having chosen \(\beta\), choose \(\alpha\in\mathbb R^{d_W}\) outside the finitely many hyperplanes
\[
 \left\{\alpha:\alpha^{\mathsf T}\bigl((\beta^{\mathsf T}u_\ell)u_k-(\beta^{\mathsf T}u_k)u_\ell\bigr)=0\right\},\qquad k<\ell.
\]
Every displayed normal vector is nonzero because \(u_k,u_\ell\) are linearly independent and both \(\beta^{\mathsf T}u_k\) and \(\beta^{\mathsf T}u_\ell\) are nonzero.  The choices exist because a finite union of proper linear hyperplanes cannot cover \(\mathbb R^{d_W}\): the product of their defining nonzero linear forms is a nonzero polynomial, while a nonzero real polynomial cannot vanish at every point (the latter follows by induction on the number of variables from the one-variable root bound).

Put
\[
 b=\sum_{q=1}^{d_W}\beta_qw^q,\qquad
 a=\sum_{q=1}^{d_W}\alpha_qw^q,\qquad
 \rho_k=\frac{a_k}{b_k}.
\]
The choice of \(\beta\) gives \(b_k\ne0\) for every \(k\), and the choice of \(\alpha\) gives \(\rho_k\ne\rho_\ell\) for \(k\ne\ell\).  By (1), both
\[
 G=Q\operatorname{diag}(a)Q^{\mathsf T}\quad\text{and}\quad
 K=Q\operatorname{diag}(b)Q^{\mathsf T}
\]
are diagonal.  Moreover, \(K\) is invertible because \(Q\) and \(\operatorname{diag}(b)\) are invertible.  Hence
\[
 GK^{-1}
 =Q\operatorname{diag}(\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_p)Q^{-1} \tag{2}
\]
is diagonal.  The eigenvalues on the right of (2) are pairwise distinct.  The eigenspaces of the diagonal matrix on the left are therefore the coordinate axes, so every column of \(Q\) is supported on exactly one coordinate.  Since \(Q\) is invertible, it is monomial: there are a permutation \(\pi\) and nonzero scalars \(q_i\) such that
\[
 Q_{i,\pi(i)}=q_i,\qquad Q_{ij}=0\quad(j\ne\pi(i)). \tag{3}
\]

It remains to remove the monomial ambiguity.  By \(\operatorname{diag}(D^{(1)})=\operatorname{diag}(D^{(2)})=\mathbf 1\), which is part of \(\text{def:admissible-matrices}\), equations \(D^{(2)}=QD^{(1)}\) and (3) imply
\[
 1=D^{(2)}_{ii}=q_iD^{(1)}_{\pi(i),i}. \tag{4}
\]
If \(\pi\) had a nontrivial cycle \(i_1,\ldots,i_d\), with \(d\ge2\) and \(\pi(i_t)=i_{t+1}\) cyclically, then (4) would give
\[
 \prod_{t=1}^d\left|D^{(1)}_{i_{t+1},i_t}\right|
 =\prod_{t=1}^d|q_{i_t}|^{-1}. \tag{5}
\]
The entries on the left of (5) form a directed simple cycle of \(I_p-D^{(1)}\), while
\[
 D^{(2)}_{i_t,i_{t+1}}
 =q_{i_t}D^{(1)}_{i_{t+1},i_{t+1}}=q_{i_t}
\]
form the reverse directed simple cycle of \(I_p-D^{(2)}\).  The two strict cycle-product inequalities in \(\text{def:admissible-matrices}\) would consequently imply both
\[
 \prod_{t=1}^d|q_{i_t}|^{-1}<1
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \prod_{t=1}^d|q_{i_t}|<1,
\]
whose product is the contradiction \(1<1\).  Thus \(\pi\) is the identity.  Equation (4) and \(D^{(1)}_{ii}=1\) then give \(q_i=1\) for every \(i\).  Hence \(Q=I_p\) and \(D^{(1)}=D^{(2)}\), as claimed.

statements.statement: Fix an honest BACKSHIFT instance \(D,H,s,\Omega\) with \(D\in\mathcal D\), nonnegative shifts, \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{+}^{p}\), and positive-definite honest covariances. If \(\delta_H>c\), equivalently \(\gamma_H>0\), then \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)=\{D\}\) for every assignment of matrices in \(\mathbb S_{++}^{p}\) to the \(c\) slots in \(E\setminus H\). If, in addition, this fixed instance has \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{++}^{p}\) and \(\delta_H\le c\), then there are positive-definite values for all slots in \(E\setminus H\), a matrix \(D'\in\mathcal D\) with \(D'\ne D\), an invariant \(\Omega'\in\mathbb S_{++}^{p}\), and nonnegative shifts on a set \(H'\subseteq E\) with \(|H'|=h\) such that \(D,D'\in\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\). Consequently, over the published class allowing \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{+}^{p}\), the threshold \(\delta_H>c\) is minimax sharp: whenever \(\delta_H\le c\), the class contains an ambiguity witness in its positive-definite invariant-noise subclass. No ambiguity is asserted for every fixed singular boundary value of \(\Omega\). On the positive-definite invariant-noise interior and at \(c=0\), the equivalence is exactly the BACKSHIFT pairwise noncollinearity criterion.
statements.justification: The theorem gives full published-class sufficiency and the exact minimax number of whole covariance environments that population BACKSHIFT can lose, with pointwise necessity stated only where its interior deformation is valid.
statements.gap: Published BACKSHIFT gives the all-honest criterion, while threshold-trimming joint diagonalization does not provide a worst-case whole-slot replacement radius, a legal contamination, or the distinction between boundary sufficiency and interior pointwise necessity.
statements.consumer: Investigators obtain an exact design audit: passing the distance test certifies every positive-semidefinite invariant-noise instance, while failing it rules out a uniform class guarantee through an explicit positive-definite ambiguity witness.
statements.proof_tex:
The causal structural target is \(D\), and hence \(B=I_p-D\); the observable-law recovery map is the set \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\) in \(\text{def:compatible-set}\).  We prove their stated relationship rather than identifying them by definition.

First suppose that \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_+^p\) and \(\delta_H>c\), and fix an arbitrary assignment of positive-definite matrices to the \(c\) slots in \(E\setminus H\).  The honest covariance equation from \(\text{ass:honest-covariance-model}\), the nonnegativity in \(\text{ass:nonnegative-shifts}\), the local premise \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_+^p\), and \(D\in\mathcal D\) from \(\text{ass:backshift-normalization}\) permit the choices
\[
 K=H,\qquad \Psi=\Omega,\qquad t_e=s_e
\]
in \(\text{def:compatible-set}\).  Therefore \(D\in\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\).  Notice that this step uses positive semidefiniteness, not the strict-interior hypothesis \(\text{ass:invariant-noise-interior}\).

Take any \(A\in\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\).  By the corrected domain statement in \(\text{def:compatible-set}\), there are \(K\subseteq E\), \(|K|\ge h\), \(\Psi\in\mathbb S_+^p\), and \(t_e\in[0,\infty)^p\) such that
\[
 \Sigma_e=A^{-1}\{\Psi+\operatorname{diag}(t_e)\}A^{-\mathsf T}
 \quad(e\in K). \tag{1}
\]
The overlap \(J=H\cap K\) obeys the inclusion--exclusion bound
\[
 |J|=|H|+|K|-|H\cup K|
 \ge h+h-m=h-c. \tag{2}
\]
By \(\text{def:environment-distance}\) and \(\text{def:max-line-occupancy}\),
\[
 \delta_H>c
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 M_{k\ell}<h-c\quad\text{for every }1\le k<\ell\le p. \tag{3}
\]
If the points \(\{(s_{ek},s_{e\ell}):e\in J\}\) were contained in an affine line for some \(k<\ell\), that line would contain at least \(|J|\ge h-c\) indexed honest points, contradicting (3).  Thus every pairwise cloud on \(J\) is noncollinear.  Equations (1), \(\text{ass:honest-covariance-model}\), the two positive-semidefinite invariant nuisances, the two nonnegative shift families, and membership of \(D,A\) in \(\mathcal D\) verify every premise of \(\text{lem:overlap-uniqueness}\).  That lemma yields \(A=D\).  Hence
\[
 \mathcal R_c(\Sigma)=\{D\}. \tag{4}
\]
No value outside \(H\) entered the argument, so (4) holds for every allowed replacement assignment and for every positive-semidefinite \(\Omega\) producing the stipulated positive-definite honest covariances.

We next prove the equivalence with the quantitative affine-minor margin.  Put \(q=h-c\).  Any family of \(h\) indexed points has at least \(\min(2,h)\) indexed points on an affine line, so
\[
 M_{k\ell}\ge \min(2,h). \tag{5}
\]
Therefore (3) is impossible when \(q<3\), precisely the case where \(\text{def:affine-separation}\) sets \(\gamma_H=0\).  Suppose \(q\ge3\).  For fixed \(S\subseteq H\) with \(|S|=q\), the points \((s_{ek},s_{e\ell})\), \(e\in S\), lie on one affine line if and only if the matrix with rows \((1,s_{ek},s_{e\ell})\) has rank at most two.  By the elementary rank criterion, this is equivalent to the vanishing of every three-by-three minor
\[
 \det\!\begin{pmatrix}
 1&s_{ek}&s_{e\ell}\\
 1&s_{fk}&s_{f\ell}\\
 1&s_{gk}&s_{g\ell}
 \end{pmatrix},
 \qquad e<f<g,\quad e,f,g\in S. \tag{6}
\]
The index collections are finite.  Hence the minimum in \(\text{def:affine-separation}\) is positive exactly when no pairwise affine line contains \(q\) honest indices.  Equivalently,
\[
 \gamma_H>0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 M_{k\ell}<q\ \text{for every }k<\ell
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \delta_H>c. \tag{7}
\]

It remains to prove the pointwise converse under the strict-interior hypothesis.  Fix \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{++}^p\) as in \(\text{ass:invariant-noise-interior}\), suppose \(\delta_H\le c\), and retain \(q=h-c=m-2c\).

If \(q\le0\), then \(|E\setminus H|=c\ge h\).  Choose \(H'\subseteq E\setminus H\) with \(|H'|=h\), fix distinct \(k,\ell\), and let \(E_{k\ell}\) have its only nonzero entry, equal to one, in position \((k,\ell)\).  For a sufficiently small nonzero \(\varepsilon\), set
\[
 D'=D+\varepsilon E_{k\ell}. \tag{8}
\]
The diagonal of \(D'\) is one.  Since determinant is continuous and \(D\) is invertible, \(D'\) is invertible for small \(|\varepsilon|\).  Since \(\operatorname{CP}(I_p-\cdot)\) is the maximum of finitely many absolute cycle-product polynomials, it is continuous; the strict inequality \(\operatorname{CP}(I_p-D)<1\) therefore persists.  Thus \(D'\in\mathcal D\), and invertibility of \(D\) together with \(\varepsilon\ne0\) gives \(D'\ne D\).  Set \(\Omega'=I_p\) and, for every replaced slot, assign
\[
 \Sigma_e=(D')^{-1}\Omega'(D')^{-\mathsf T}. \tag{9}
\]
These matrices are positive definite by invertible congruence.  The original explanation fits \(H\), while \((D',\Omega')\) with zero shifts fits \(H'\).  The definition of \(\mathcal R_c\) then gives \(D,D'\in\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\).

Suppose now that \(q>0\).  From \(\delta_H\le c\), \(\text{def:environment-distance}\), and \(\text{def:max-line-occupancy}\), there are \(k<\ell\), an affine line \(L\), and \(S\subseteq H\) with \(|S|=q\) whose \((k,\ell)\)-shift points lie on \(L\).  Choose a nonzero direction \(v=(v_k,v_\ell)\) of \(L\), fix \(e_0\in S\), and define scalars \(\tau_e\) by
\[
 (s_{ek}-s_{e_0k},s_{e\ell}-s_{e_0\ell})
 =\tau_e(v_k,v_\ell),\qquad e\in S. \tag{10}
\]
For real \(\varepsilon\), put
\[
 \eta_k(\varepsilon)=1+\varepsilon v_kD_{\ell k},
 \qquad
 \eta_\ell(\varepsilon)=1-\varepsilon v_\ell D_{k\ell}, \tag{11}
\]
and let \(Q_\varepsilon\) equal the identity outside its \(k,\ell\) principal block, where
\[
 (Q_\varepsilon)_{\{k,\ell\},\{k,\ell\}}
 =\begin{pmatrix}
 \eta_k(\varepsilon)^{-1}&\varepsilon v_k\eta_k(\varepsilon)^{-1}\\
 -\varepsilon v_\ell\eta_\ell(\varepsilon)^{-1}&\eta_\ell(\varepsilon)^{-1}
 \end{pmatrix}. \tag{12}
\]
At \(\varepsilon=0\), both denominators and the determinant of \(Q_\varepsilon\) equal one.  They remain nonzero in a neighborhood of zero.  Define \(D'_\varepsilon=Q_\varepsilon D\).  Using \(D_{kk}=D_{\ell\ell}=1\) from \(\text{ass:backshift-normalization}\),
\[
 (D'_\varepsilon)_{kk}
 =\frac{1+\varepsilon v_kD_{\ell k}}{\eta_k(\varepsilon)}=1,
 \qquad
 (D'_\varepsilon)_{\ell\ell}
 =\frac{1-\varepsilon v_\ell D_{k\ell}}{\eta_\ell(\varepsilon)}=1, \tag{13}
\]
and every other diagonal entry remains one.  The same continuity argument used after (8) shows that \(D'_\varepsilon\in\mathcal D\) for all sufficiently small \(|\varepsilon|\).  Because \(v\ne0\), (12) has a nonzero off-diagonal entry for every sufficiently small nonzero \(\varepsilon\); hence \(Q_\varepsilon\ne I_p\), and invertibility of \(D\) implies \(D'_\varepsilon\ne D\).

For \(x_e=s_e-s_{e_0}\), direct multiplication of the block (12), followed by (10), gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 [Q_\varepsilon\operatorname{diag}(x_e)Q_\varepsilon^{\mathsf T}]_{k\ell}
 &=\frac{-\varepsilon v_\ell x_{ek}+\varepsilon v_kx_{e\ell}}
 {\eta_k(\varepsilon)\eta_\ell(\varepsilon)}\\
 &=\frac{-\varepsilon v_\ell\tau_ev_k+\varepsilon v_k\tau_ev_\ell}
 {\eta_k(\varepsilon)\eta_\ell(\varepsilon)}=0.
 \end{aligned} \tag{14}
\]
Every other off-diagonal entry vanishes because \(Q_\varepsilon\) is block diagonal with an identity complement.  Consequently
\[
 C_\varepsilon
 =\operatorname{off}\!\left(Q_\varepsilon\operatorname{diag}(s_e)Q_\varepsilon^{\mathsf T}\right),
 \qquad \operatorname{off}(G)=G-\operatorname{diag}(\operatorname{diag}(G)), \tag{15}
\]
is independent of \(e\in S\).  Define
\[
 \Omega'_\varepsilon=Q_\varepsilon\Omega Q_\varepsilon^{\mathsf T}+C_\varepsilon. \tag{16}
\]
The matrix in (16) is symmetric and depends continuously on \(\varepsilon\).  At zero it equals \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{++}^p\).  Openness of the positive-definite cone therefore permits a sufficiently small nonzero \(\varepsilon\) for which, simultaneously,
\[
 D'=D'_\varepsilon\in\mathcal D,\qquad D'\ne D,\qquad
 \Omega'=\Omega'_\varepsilon\in\mathbb S_{++}^p. \tag{17}
\]
For \(e\in S\) and \(1\le i\le p\), set
\[
 t_{ei}
 =[Q_\varepsilon\operatorname{diag}(s_e)Q_\varepsilon^{\mathsf T}]_{ii}
 =\sum_{j=1}^p(Q_\varepsilon)_{ij}^2s_{ej}\ge0, \tag{18}
\]
where the inequality follows from \(\text{ass:nonnegative-shifts}\).  Equations (15)--(18) and \(\text{ass:honest-covariance-model}\) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 D'\Sigma_eD'^{\mathsf T}
 &=Q_\varepsilon\{\Omega+\operatorname{diag}(s_e)\}Q_\varepsilon^{\mathsf T}\\
 &=\Omega'+\operatorname{diag}(t_e),
 \qquad e\in S. 
 \end{aligned} \tag{19}
\]
Let \(H'=S\cup(E\setminus H)\).  The sets are disjoint and
\[
 |H'|=q+c=h. \tag{20}
\]
Assign each replaced slot the covariance
\[
 \Sigma_e=(D')^{-1}\Omega'(D')^{-\mathsf T},
 \qquad e\in E\setminus H. \tag{21}
\]
It is positive definite by (17) and invertible congruence.  Equations (18)--(21) show that \(D'\) fits all slots of \(H'\), with zero shifts on \(E\setminus H\), whereas \(D\) continues to fit \(H\).  Hence \(D,D'\in\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\), which proves the fixed-interior-instance converse.

The published BACKSHIFT second-moment class permits every \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_+^p\) and therefore contains the strict subclass \(\mathbb S_{++}^p\).  For any design with \(\delta_H\le c\), the preceding construction may be run at, for example, \(\Omega=I_p\).  Thus a uniform guarantee over the published class fails below the threshold.  This proves minimax sharpness over that class while making no assertion about a preassigned singular \(\Omega\).  Finally, on the positive-definite interior and with \(c=0\), \(h=m\) and
\[
 \delta_H>0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 M_{k\ell}<h\ \text{for every }k<\ell,
\]
which is exactly that no complete pairwise shift cloud is contained in an affine line, the stated BACKSHIFT noncollinearity criterion.

statements.statement: Under the prespecified support pattern \(Z\) and absolutely continuous active amplitudes, simultaneously for every \(k<\ell\), \(M_{k\ell}=M_{k\ell}^{\mathrm{gen}}\) almost surely. Consequently, the pattern guarantees \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)=\{D\}\) uniformly for all admissible \(D\in\mathcal D\), all \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{+}^{p}\) producing positive-definite honest covariances, and every positive-definite assignment to the \(c\) replacement slots if and only if, for every \(k<\ell\), \(\max\{n_{00}^{k\ell}+n_{10}^{k\ell},n_{00}^{k\ell}+n_{01}^{k\ell},n_{00}^{k\ell}+\mathbf 1\{n_{11}^{k\ell}>0\},\min(2,h)\}<h-c\). Failure of this inequality has an ambiguity witness with positive-definite invariant noise; it is not a claim that every fixed singular boundary instance is ambiguous. In particular, any uniformly robustly identifying support pattern satisfies \(m\ge2c+3\), and this environment-count lower bound is attained by support patterns with no larger forced affine incidence.
statements.justification: The exact four-term formula turns a support hypergraph into a uniform published-class design threshold and exposes the unavoidable \(2c+3\) environment floor.
statements.gap: Existing generic-amplitude and sparse-shift results do not compute affine-line occupancy under whole-environment replacement or distinguish uniform class necessity from pointwise behavior at singular invariant-noise boundaries.
statements.consumer: Experimental planners can select intervention targets so the realized sparse design tolerates a prespecified number of arbitrary failed environments uniformly over the published second-moment class.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(k<\ell\), and write
\[
 P_e=(s_{ek},s_{e\ell})=(Z_{ek}a_{ek},Z_{e\ell}a_{e\ell}),
 \qquad e\in H, \tag{22}
\]
using \(\text{ass:support-factorization}\).  The support types \(00,10,01,11\) put \(P_e\), respectively, at the origin, on the positive horizontal axis, on the positive vertical axis, and in the open positive quadrant.

The horizontal and vertical axes have respective indexed occupancies
\[
 n_{00}^{k\ell}+n_{10}^{k\ell}
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 n_{00}^{k\ell}+n_{01}^{k\ell}. \tag{23}
\]
If \(n_{11}^{k\ell}>0\), the line through the origin and any one \(11\) point has occupancy at least \(n_{00}^{k\ell}+1\).  Any two indexed points lie on an affine line, including when the two coordinates coincide.  Thus
\[
 M_{k\ell}\ge
 \max\!\left\{
 n_{00}^{k\ell}+n_{10}^{k\ell},
 n_{00}^{k\ell}+n_{01}^{k\ell},
 n_{00}^{k\ell}+\mathbf 1\{n_{11}^{k\ell}>0\},
 \min(2,h)
 \right\}. \tag{24}
\]

We prove the reverse inequality outside a null set.  Write \(P_r=(x_r,y_r)\).  For two nonzero-support points, collinearity with the origin is the polynomial equation
\[
 x_ey_f-x_fy_e=0. \tag{25}
\]
Except when both points have type \(10\), or both have type \(01\), the polynomial in (25) is not identically zero on the active coordinates: mixed axis types give a nonzero product, an axis type paired with type \(11\) gives a nonzero product, and two type \(11\) points give two distinct monomials.  For three nonzero-support points, collinearity is
\[
 \det\!\begin{pmatrix}
 1&x_e&y_e\\
 1&x_f&y_f\\
 1&x_g&y_g
 \end{pmatrix}=0. \tag{26}
\]
Unless all three support types are \(10\), or all three are \(01\), this determinant polynomial is not identically zero.  Indeed, two horizontal points and a vertical or interior point can be chosen noncollinear, as can the coordinate-swapped configuration; the remaining mixed cases admit one point off the line through the other two; and three interior points may be chosen as \((1,1),(1,2),(2,1)\).  Equality of two active coordinates belonging to distinct type \(10\) points, or to distinct type \(01\) points, is likewise the zero set of a nonzero linear polynomial.

For completeness, the zero set of a nonzero real polynomial has Lebesgue measure zero.  This follows by induction on its number of variables: the one-variable assertion follows from finiteness of roots; in the induction step, expand in the last variable, discard the null set where every coefficient vanishes by the induction hypothesis, and use finitely many roots on each remaining section.  Integrating these null sections gives a null set.  There are finitely many coordinate pairs and indexed pairs and triples.  Joint absolute continuity in \(\text{ass:generic-active-amplitudes}\) therefore implies that, simultaneously for every \(k<\ell\), none of the accidental equations above holds almost surely.

On this probability-one event, a line through the origin that contains a type \(10\) point is the horizontal axis and has the first occupancy in (23); the analogous statement for type \(01\) gives the second.  A line through the origin containing neither axis type has at most one type \(11\) point by (25), so its occupancy is at most \(n_{00}^{k\ell}+\mathbf 1\{n_{11}^{k\ell}>0\}\).  A line not through the origin contains no type \(00\) point.  If it contained three indices, (26) would force all three to have type \(10\) or all three to have type \(01\), but their line would then be an axis through the origin.  Hence its occupancy is at most \(\min(2,h)\).  Together with (24), this proves
\[
 M_{k\ell}
 =\max\!\left\{
 n_{00}^{k\ell}+n_{10}^{k\ell},
 n_{00}^{k\ell}+n_{01}^{k\ell},
 n_{00}^{k\ell}+\mathbf 1\{n_{11}^{k\ell}>0\},
 \min(2,h)
 \right\}
 =M_{k\ell}^{\mathrm{gen}} \tag{27}
\]
simultaneously for all \(k<\ell\), almost surely.

By \(\text{def:environment-distance}\),
\[
 \delta_H>c
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 M_{k\ell}<h-c\quad\text{for every }k<\ell. \tag{28}
\]
Substituting (27) into (28) gives the four-term criterion.  If it holds, the positive-semidefinite sufficiency part of \(\text{thm:sharp-replacement-radius}\) proves uniqueness for every admissible published-class instance and every replacement.  If it fails, then \(\delta_H\le c\); choosing an invariant covariance in \(\mathbb S_{++}^p\), the pointwise converse in that theorem supplies a legal ambiguity.  Thus the criterion is necessary and sufficient for a uniform guarantee over the published positive-semidefinite class, without asserting failure for each singular boundary instance.

The term \(\min(2,h)\) makes the strict inequality in (28) possible only if \(h-c\ge3\).  Since \(h=m-c\),
\[
 m\ge2c+3. \tag{29}
\]
This lower bound is attained.  If \(m=2c+3\), take the all-active pattern \(Z_{ek}=1\).  Then, for every \(k<\ell\),
\[
 n_{11}^{k\ell}=h,\qquad
 n_{00}^{k\ell}=n_{10}^{k\ell}=n_{01}^{k\ell}=0,\qquad
 M_{k\ell}^{\mathrm{gen}}=2<h-c=3. \tag{30}
\]
Hence the all-active pattern gives uniform robust identification almost surely at the smallest possible environment count.

statements.statement:
The definition-level coverage claim is valid, but the requested computable confidence-union construction has a negative answer for the region class stated in the question.  More precisely, if
\[
G_{n,\alpha,H}=\{\Sigma_e\in\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\text{ for every }e\in H\},
\]
then \(G_{n,\alpha,H}\subseteq\{D\in\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\}\), and consequently \(\Pr(G_{n,\alpha,H})\ge 1-\alpha\) implies \(\Pr\{D\in\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\}\ge1-\alpha\).

For a rational population covariance family \(\Sigma\), the population compatibility set \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\) has an exact rational semialgebraic description.  Effective real quantifier elimination therefore supplies finite rational-polynomial certificates for infeasibility, singleton output, and multiple-candidate output.  The affine minors of the fitted diagonal shifts can be included, without division, among the sign polynomials in each certificate.  These minors certify separation, but they cannot by themselves certify feasibility: the covariance equations, positive-semidefinite invariant nuisance, nonnegative shifts, invertibility, unit diagonal, and cycle-product inequalities are also necessary.  Normalization-chart changes are sound when pivot nonvanishing and all normalization and cycle inequalities are cleared to polynomial sign conditions before a chart certificate is accepted.

In contrast, when \(\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\) is only an arbitrary nonempty subset of \(\mathbb S_{++}^p\), as in the frozen definition, no deterministic procedure making only finitely many membership queries to these sets can return the exact full set \(\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\) for every region family.  This failure already occurs for \(p=2\), \(m=3\), and \(c=0\), with rational positive-definite matrices and a design having affine-minor separation \(\gamma_H=1\).  Hence the complete conjunction requested in the open question is false as stated: an exact computable confidence union, and thus a computable full-output-or-abstain rule at \(\gamma_H=0\), requires an additional effective representation of the regions.  The causal target remains \(B=I_p-D\); neither the coverage inclusion nor the semialgebraic description defines that target to equal an observable functional.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Coverage.}
Fix \(n\geq 1\), \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), and a sample outcome in \(G_{n,\alpha,H}\).  For \(e\in H\), set \(\Gamma_e=\Sigma_e\).  For each \(e\in E\setminus H\), choose \(\Gamma_e\in\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\); this finite choice is possible because every region is nonempty by the declared type of \(\mathcal C^{(n)}_\alpha\).  Every \(\Gamma_e\) is positive definite because every region is a subset of \(\mathbb S_{++}^p\).  In the compatibility definition take
\[
 A=D,\qquad K=H,\qquad \Psi=\Omega,\qquad t_e=s_e\quad(e\in H).
\]
The cardinality condition \(|K|=h\) follows from the definition of \(H\).  The BACKSHIFT-normalization assumption gives \(D\in\mathcal D\); the invariant-noise-interior assumption gives \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{++}^p\subseteq\mathbb S_+^p\); and the nonnegative-shifts assumption gives \(s_e\in[0,\infty)^p\).  Finally, for every \(e\in K=H\), the honest-covariance-model assumption and the choice of \(\Gamma_e\) give
\[
 \Gamma_e=\Sigma_e
 =D^{-1}\bigl(\Omega+\operatorname{diag}(s_e)\bigr)D^{-\mathsf T}.
\]
Thus all conjuncts in \(\text{def:compatible-set}\) hold, so \(D\in\mathcal R_c(\Gamma)\).  Since this \(\Gamma\) is one of the families in the union in \(\text{def:confidence-union}\),
\[
 G_{n,\alpha,H}\subseteq\{D\in\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\}.
\]
Monotonicity of probability therefore yields
\[
 \Pr\{D\in\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\}
 \geq \Pr(G_{n,\alpha,H})\geq 1-\alpha.
\]

\textbf{Exact rational semialgebraic representation.}
Suppose every entry of every \(\Sigma_e\) is rational.  It is enough to enumerate sets \(K\subseteq E\) of cardinality exactly \(h\): a witness on a set of size at least \(h\) restricts to any \(h\)-element subset, and a witness on an \(h\)-element set already satisfies the definition.  This is precisely the finite subset reduction named in \(\text{def:subset-consensus}\).

Fix such a set \(K\).  Introduce real variables \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}\), a symmetric real matrix \(\Psi\), and \(t_e\in\mathbb R^p\) for \(e\in K\).  The following is a first-order formula over the ordered real field:
\[
\begin{aligned}
 F_K(A,\Psi,t)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 &A_{ii}=1 &&(1\leq i\leq p),\\
 &(\det A)^2>0,\\
 &1-\pi_C(A)>0\ \text{ and }\ 1+\pi_C(A)>0
   &&(C\text{ a directed simple cycle}),\\
 &\Psi=\Psi^{\mathsf T},\qquad
   v^{\mathsf T}\Psi v\geq0 &&(v\in\mathbb R^p),\\
 &t_{ej}\geq0 &&(e\in K,\ 1\leq j\leq p),\\
 &A\Sigma_eA^{\mathsf T}=\Psi+\operatorname{diag}(t_e)
   &&(e\in K).
\end{aligned}
\]
Here \(\pi_C(A)\) is the product of the entries of \(I_p-A\) along \(C\).  There are only finitely many directed simple cycles.  By the definition of \(\operatorname{CP}\), their two strict inequalities are equivalent to \(\operatorname{CP}(I_p-A)<1\).  The determinant inequality is equivalent to invertibility.  The universally quantified quadratic-form inequalities are exactly the definition of \(\Psi\in\mathbb S_+^p\).  All displayed atoms are polynomial sign conditions with rational coefficients, because \(\Sigma_e\) is rational.

If \(F_K(A,\Psi,t)\) holds, invertibility permits multiplication of its last equality by \(A^{-1}\) and \(A^{-\mathsf T}\), giving
\[
 \Sigma_e=A^{-1}\bigl(\Psi+\operatorname{diag}(t_e)\bigr)A^{-\mathsf T}
 \quad(e\in K).
\]
Thus \(A\) is compatible.  Conversely, multiplying each covariance equality in \(\text{def:compatible-set}\) by \(A\) and \(A^{\mathsf T}\) gives \(F_K\).  Consequently the exact recovery set is
\[
 \mathcal R_c(\Sigma)
 =\bigcup_{\substack{K\subseteq E\\ |K|=h}}
   \left\{A:\exists\Psi\,\exists(t_e:e\in K)\ F_K(A,\Psi,t)\right\}.
\]
The union is finite.  Applying \(\text{lem:effective-real-quantifier-elimination}\) to the displayed formula produces an effectively computable quantifier-free Boolean combination \(\varphi_\Sigma(A)\) of rational-polynomial sign conditions whose solution set is exactly \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\).

For completeness, put
\[
 d(A,A')=\sum_{i=1}^p\sum_{j=1}^p(A_{ij}-A'_{ij})^2.
\]
The three mutually relevant output assertions are expressed exactly by
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathsf{Empty}&:\quad \neg\exists A\,\varphi_\Sigma(A),\\
 \mathsf{Singleton}&:\quad
   \exists A\left[\varphi_\Sigma(A)\wedge
   \forall A'\bigl(\varphi_\Sigma(A')\Rightarrow d(A,A')=0\bigr)\right],\\
 \mathsf{Multiple}&:\quad
   \exists A\,\exists A'\left[
   \varphi_\Sigma(A)\wedge\varphi_\Sigma(A')\wedge d(A,A')>0\right].
\end{aligned}
\]
Each is again a first-order ordered-field formula with rational-polynomial atoms.  A second application of \(\text{lem:effective-real-quantifier-elimination}\) gives a finite rational-polynomial sign certificate deciding each assertion.  The singleton formula includes existence, so it does not confuse an empty set with a set having at most one point.

For every \(e<f<g\) in \(K\) and \(k<\ell\), define the fitted-shift minor
\[
 \Delta_{efg}^{k\ell}(t)=
 \det\begin{pmatrix}
 1&t_{ek}&t_{e\ell}\\
 1&t_{fk}&t_{f\ell}\\
 1&t_{gk}&t_{g\ell}
 \end{pmatrix}.
\]
It is a polynomial, so all atoms \(\Delta_{efg}^{k\ell}(t)=0\), \(\Delta_{efg}^{k\ell}(t)>0\), and \(-\Delta_{efg}^{k\ell}(t)>0\) may be added to the finite sign family before elimination; no ratio is introduced.  For a set of at least three fitted profiles, some such determinant is nonzero exactly when those profiles are not contained in one affine line: a nonzero determinant gives three affinely independent points, whereas if all determinants vanish then the affine span has dimension at most one.  Hence these atoms certify affine separation.  They do not certify feasibility by themselves.  For example, the profiles \((0,0),(1,0),(0,1)\) have determinant one regardless of whether a proposed matrix has unit diagonal or whether a proposed invariant matrix is positive semidefinite.  The covariance equations, quadratic-form inequalities for \(\Psi\), nonnegativity of \(t\), determinant inequality, unit-diagonal equations, and all cycle-product inequalities in \(F_K\) remain separate necessary conjuncts.

The same representation also proves the chart assertion.  Let \(C\) be a raw diagonalizer in a normalization chart, set \(q_i=C_{ii}\), and suppose \(q_i\neq0\) for all \(i\).  Introduce the normalized matrix \(A\) by the polynomial relations
\[
 q_iA_{ij}=C_{ij},\qquad q_i=C_{ii},\qquad q_i^2>0.
\]
Then \(A_{ii}=1\) and \(A=\operatorname{diag}(q_1,\ldots,q_p)^{-1}C\).  Invertibility is encoded by \((\det C)^2>0\).  If a cycle product becomes \(N_C(C)/Q_C(q)\), where \(Q_C(q)\neq0\), then
\[
 \left|\frac{N_C(C)}{Q_C(q)}\right|<1
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 Q_C(q)^2-N_C(C)^2>0.
\]
Covariance equalities are cleared by multiplying by the relevant nonzero pivot products, while inequalities are cleared with positive squared denominators.  Thus pivot nonvanishing together with the polynomial normalization, invertibility, covariance, and cycle conditions is equivalent to the normalized chart conditions.  Omitting any of them would enlarge the projected set and would not be a sound chart certificate.

\textbf{Finite-membership-query obstruction.}
It remains to show that arbitrary confidence regions do not supply enough information for exact computation.  Consider
\[
 p=2,\qquad m=h=3,\qquad c=0,\qquad H=E=\{1,2,3\},
\]
and take
\[
 D=I_2,\qquad \Omega=2I_2,\qquad
 s_1=(0,0),\quad s_2=(1,0),\quad s_3=(0,1).
\]
These choices satisfy the normalization, strict invariant-noise positivity, and nonnegative-shift assumptions.  The honest-covariance equation gives the rational positive-definite matrices
\[
 \Sigma_1=\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\0&2\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 \Sigma_2=\begin{pmatrix}3&0\\0&2\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 \Sigma_3=\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\0&3\end{pmatrix}.
\]
There is one coordinate pair and one three-element subset in \(\text{def:affine-separation}\), and
\[
 \gamma_H=left|
 \det\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\1&1&0\\1&0&1\end{pmatrix}
 \right|=1.
\]

We first compute the baseline compatibility set.  Let \(A\in\mathcal R_0(\Sigma)\).  Since \(h=m=3\), the compatible subset must be all of \(E\).  Unit diagonal writes
\[
 A=\begin{pmatrix}1&x\\y&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Subtracting the transformed covariance equation for environment one from those for environments two and three cancels the common \(\Psi\) and gives diagonal matrices.  Their off-diagonal entries are therefore zero.  Direct multiplication gives
\[
 A(\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1)A^{\mathsf T}
 =A\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}A^{\mathsf T}
 =\begin{pmatrix}1&y\\y&y^2\end{pmatrix},
\]
so \(y=0\), and
\[
 A(\Sigma_3-\Sigma_1)A^{\mathsf T}
 =A\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}A^{\mathsf T}
 =\begin{pmatrix}x^2&x\\x&1\end{pmatrix},
\]
so \(x=0\).  Hence every compatible \(A\) is \(I_2\).  Conversely, \(I_2\) is compatible with \(\Psi=2I_2\) and the displayed nonnegative shifts.  Therefore
\[
 \mathcal R_0(\Sigma)=\{I_2\}.
\]

For any nonzero rational number \(q\), define
\[
 A_q=\begin{pmatrix}1&q\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 \Psi_q=A_q\Sigma_1A_q^{\mathsf T}
 =2\begin{pmatrix}1+q^2&q\\q&1\end{pmatrix},
\]
and
\[
 \Gamma_{3,q}
 =A_q^{-1}\bigl(\Psi_q+\operatorname{diag}(0,1)\bigr)A_q^{-\mathsf T}
 =\begin{pmatrix}2+q^2&-q\\-q&3\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The matrix \(A_q\) is invertible, has unit diagonal, and \(I_2-A_q\) has zero product around its only directed two-cycle; hence \(A_q\in\mathcal D\).  The matrix \(\Psi_q\) is positive definite because it is the congruence of \(2I_2\) by the invertible matrix \(A_q\).  Moreover, \(\Gamma_{3,q}\) is positive definite since its leading diagonal entry is positive and
\[
 \det(\Gamma_{3,q})=3(2+q^2)-q^2=6+2q^2>0.
\]
The first column of \(A_q\) is \((1,0)^{\mathsf T}\), so
\[
 A_q\Sigma_1A_q^{\mathsf T}=\Psi_q,
 \qquad
 A_q\Sigma_2A_q^{\mathsf T}=\Psi_q+\operatorname{diag}(1,0),
 \qquad
 A_q\Gamma_{3,q}A_q^{\mathsf T}=\Psi_q+\operatorname{diag}(0,1).
\]
Thus \(A_q\in\mathcal R_0(\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2,\Gamma_{3,q})\), with an invariant nuisance that is positive definite and shifts that are nonnegative.  All entries are rational, and \(A_q\neq I_2\).

Now suppose, for contradiction, that a deterministic procedure always returns the exact confidence union after finitely many membership queries to each region.  Run it on the nonempty singleton regions
\[
 \mathcal C^0_1=\{\Sigma_1\},\qquad
 \mathcal C^0_2=\{\Sigma_2\},\qquad
 \mathcal C^0_3=\{\Sigma_3\}.
\]
Its exact union is \(\mathcal U^0=\mathcal R_0(\Sigma)=\{I_2\}\).  The run asks only finitely many questions of the third membership oracle.  Because the matrices \(\Gamma_{3,q}\) are distinct as \(q\) ranges over the infinitely many nonzero rationals, choose a rational \(q\neq0\) for which \(\Gamma_{3,q}\) was not queried.  Define a second region family by
\[
 \mathcal C^1_1=\mathcal C^0_1,\qquad
 \mathcal C^1_2=\mathcal C^0_2,\qquad
 \mathcal C^1_3=\{\Sigma_3,\Gamma_{3,q}\}.
\]
Every region remains a nonempty subset of \(\mathbb S_{++}^2\), and every listed matrix is rational.  Every membership answer along the first transcript is identical for the two families: the first two regions are unchanged, and the only new member of the third region was not queried.  Induction over the deterministic query sequence therefore gives the same complete transcript and the same returned set on both inputs.  However,
\[
 A_q\in\mathcal R_0(\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2,\Gamma_{3,q})
 \subseteq\mathcal U^1,
 \qquad
 A_q\notin\mathcal U^0=\{I_2\}.
\]
The exact unions differ, a contradiction.  Hence no deterministic finite-membership-query procedure can compute the exact union for the frozen arbitrary-set region class, even at the strictly separated rational design \(\gamma_H=1\).  In particular, a rule required to return the full exact union away from \(\gamma_H=0\) and to abstain only at the boundary already fails on this example.  An effective representation of the regions is therefore necessary for the requested computable full-output-or-abstain construction.

Finally, the structural causal target was fixed independently as \(B=I_p-D\).  The coverage inclusion is a confidence statement about that target, and \(\varphi_\Sigma\) is an observed-law compatibility functional.  The preceding arguments prove their stated relationships; neither argument defines the causal target to equal an observed functional.
statements.justification: This gives the exact definition-level coverage proof, an executable symbolic population certificate for rational covariances, and an explicit witness showing why exact confidence-union computation is impossible for the frozen arbitrary-set region type.
statements.gap: The result isolates input representation as a logically prior obstruction. It leaves the analytic local-modulus problem separate rather than silently assuming a finite encoding of arbitrary confidence regions.
statements.consumer: An implementation may use the rational semialgebraic population certificate immediately, but must require an effective region representation before promising exact confidence unions or boundary-triggered abstention.

statements.statement: Every first-order formula over the ordered field of real numbers whose atomic predicates are sign conditions on finitely many polynomials with rational coefficients admits an effectively computable equivalent quantifier-free formula.  In particular, closed such formulas are decidable, and projections of rational semialgebraic sets have computable rational semialgebraic descriptions.

statements.statement:
Let \(I\) be a finite index set of cardinality \(r\), let \(Z^\circ\in\{0,1\}^{I\times p}\), and let \(a^\circ\in(0,\infty)^{I\times p}\). Suppose the subarray \((a^\circ_{ek}:Z^\circ_{ek}=1)\) has a joint distribution absolutely continuous on its positive orthant. Define \(P_e^{k\ell}=(Z^\circ_{ek}a^\circ_{ek},Z^\circ_{e\ell}a^\circ_{e\ell})\), \(N_{uv}^{k\ell}=\#\{e\in I:(Z^\circ_{ek},Z^\circ_{e\ell})=(u,v)\}\), and \(M_I^{k\ell}=\max_{L\text{ affine line}}\#\{e\in I:P_e^{k\ell}\in L\}\). Then, simultaneously for all \(k<\ell\), almost surely
\[
 M_I^{k\ell}=\max\{N_{00}^{k\ell}+N_{10}^{k\ell},N_{00}^{k\ell}+N_{01}^{k\ell},N_{00}^{k\ell}+\mathbf 1\{N_{11}^{k\ell}>0\},\min(2,r)\}.
\]
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(k<\ell\) and abbreviate \(P_e^{k\ell}=(x_e,y_e)\).  Type \(00\) gives the origin, types \(10\) and \(01\) give the two positive coordinate axes, and type \(11\) gives the open positive quadrant.  The horizontal axis, vertical axis, a line through the origin and one type \(11\) point when such a point exists, and a line through any two indexed points show
\[
 M_I^{k\ell}\ge
 \max\!\left\{
 N_{00}^{k\ell}+N_{10}^{k\ell},
 N_{00}^{k\ell}+N_{01}^{k\ell},
 N_{00}^{k\ell}+\mathbf 1\{N_{11}^{k\ell}>0\},
 \min(2,r)
 \right\}. \tag{22}
\]

For two nonzero-support points, collinearity with the origin is the polynomial equation
\[
 x_ey_f-x_fy_e=0. \tag{23}
\]
Unless both types are \(10\), or both are \(01\), this polynomial is not identically zero in the active coordinates: the mixed axis and axis--interior cases contain a nonzero product, while the interior--interior case contains two distinct monomials.  For three nonzero-support points, collinearity is the equation
\[
 \det\!\begin{pmatrix}
 1&x_e&y_e\\
 1&x_f&y_f\\
 1&x_g&y_g
 \end{pmatrix}=0. \tag{24}
\]
Except when all three types are \(10\), or all three are \(01\), this is not the zero polynomial.  To verify this, choose two distinct horizontal points and a vertical or interior point, use the coordinate-swapped construction, put one point off the line through the other two in the remaining mixed cases, and use \((1,1),(1,2),(2,1)\) for three interior points.  Equality of the active coordinates of two distinct type \(10\) points, and its type \(01\) analogue, is also the zero set of a nonzero linear polynomial.

The zero set of a nonzero polynomial in finitely many real variables has Lebesgue measure zero.  An induction proves this directly: a nonzero univariate polynomial has finitely many roots; after expansion in the last variable, the induction hypothesis removes the null set on which all coefficient polynomials vanish, every remaining section has finitely many roots, and integration of the null sections gives the result.  There are finitely many coordinate pairs and indexed pairs and triples.  Joint absolute continuity therefore gives a single probability-one event on which none of the non-forced equations (23)--(24) or coordinate equalities occurs, simultaneously for all \(k<\ell\).

On that event, a line through the origin containing type \(10\) is the horizontal axis, and the coordinate-swapped statement holds for type \(01\).  A line through the origin containing neither axis type has at most one type \(11\) point by (23).  A line not through the origin has no type \(00\) point; if it contained three indices, (24) would force all three to be type \(10\) or all three to be type \(01\), but the resulting coordinate axis passes through the origin.  Thus every line is bounded by one of the four quantities in (22), proving equality.
statements.justification: This finite-index lemma isolates the generic incidence calculation so both realized-set and ex-ante full-array design results use the same declared proof spine.
statements.gap: Sparse-support results do not provide this exact affine-line occupancy formula with repeated origin points and two forced coordinate axes.
statements.consumer: The full-array deletion-radius corollary applies the lemma before taking the worst retained subset.

statements.statement: Let \(\bar Z\in\{0,1\}^{E\times p}\) be a planned full-environment support array and let \(\bar a\in(0,\infty)^{E\times p}\). Suppose the active subarray \((\bar a_{ek}:\bar Z_{ek}=1)\) has a joint density on its positive orthant, and put \(\bar s_{ek}=\bar Z_{ek}\bar a_{ek}\). For \(u,v\in\{0,1\}\), define \(N_{uv}^{k\ell}=\#\{e\in E:(\bar Z_{ek},\bar Z_{e\ell})=(u,v)\}\), and set \(T=\max_{k<\ell}\max\{N_{00}^{k\ell}+N_{10}^{k\ell},N_{00}^{k\ell}+N_{01}^{k\ell},N_{00}^{k\ell}+\mathbf 1\{N_{11}^{k\ell}>0\},\min(2,m)\}\). Almost surely, the following are equivalent: (i) for every failed set \(F\subseteq E\) with \(|F|=c\), the retained set \(H=E\setminus F\) and shifts \((\bar s_e:e\in H)\) give a design that guarantees \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)=\{D\}\) uniformly over all admissible \(D\in\mathcal D\), all \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_+^p\) producing positive-definite honest covariances, and all positive-definite replacements; (ii) \(T<m-2c\). If \(T<m\), condition (ii) is equivalent to \(c\le\lfloor(m-T-1)/2\rfloor\); if \(T=m\), no nonnegative corruption budget is certified. For the all-active design and \(m\ge3\), the largest certified budget is \(c_{\max}=\lfloor(m-3)/2\rfloor\).
statements.justification: This corollary converts the realized honest-set radius into an ex-ante guarantee against every choice of failed environments.
statements.gap: The realized-design occupancy formula alone does not tell a planner whether every possible deletion set remains safe; the full-array statistic \(T\) closes that quantifier exactly.
statements.consumer: An experimental planner can compute one integer from the planned support array and read off the largest uniformly certified failure budget before collecting outcomes.
statements.proof_tex:
For a coordinate pair \(k<\ell\), let \(T_{k\ell}\) denote the inner four-term maximum in the definition of \(T\).  Apply \(\text{lem:generic-affine-occupancy}\) with \(I=E\) and \(r=m\).  Its joint absolute-continuity premise is exactly the amplitude premise of the corollary, so on one probability-one event the full \((k,\ell)\)-cloud has maximum affine-line occupancy \(T_{k\ell}\), simultaneously for every pair.

Fix a pair \(k<\ell\).  For a retained set \(H\subseteq E\) of size \(m-c\), write \(M_{k\ell}(H)\) for the maximum line occupancy after restriction to \(H\).  We claim
\[
 \max_{H\subseteq E:\,|H|=m-c}M_{k\ell}(H)
 =\min\{T_{k\ell},m-c\}. \tag{31}
\]
The upper bound is immediate from restriction and cardinality.  For the reverse bound, choose a line attaining the full occupancy \(T_{k\ell}\), which exists because the finite cloud determines only finitely many relevant incidences.  If \(T_{k\ell}\ge m-c\), retain any \(m-c\) indices on that line.  If \(T_{k\ell}<m-c\), retain all its \(T_{k\ell}\) indices and add any \(m-c-T_{k\ell}\) other indices.  Both constructions are feasible and prove (31).

For each retained set, \(h=m-c\).  By the published-class sufficiency and strict-interior minimax converse in \(\text{thm:sharp-replacement-radius}\), this retained design gives a uniform guarantee over the positive-semidefinite invariant-noise class exactly when
\[
 M_{k\ell}(H)<h-c=m-2c
 \quad\text{for every }k<\ell. \tag{32}
\]
Indeed, sufficiency in (32) holds for every fixed positive-semidefinite instance; if (32) fails, choosing a positive-definite invariant covariance supplies the required class member witnessing ambiguity.  Since \(m-2c\le m-c\), equations (31)--(32) show that (32) holds for every retained set if and only if
\[
 T_{k\ell}<m-2c\quad\text{for every }k<\ell,
\]
which is equivalent to \(T<m-2c\).

Because \(c\) is an integer, when \(T<m\) the strict inequality is equivalent to
\[
 2c\le m-T-1
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 c\le\left\lfloor\frac{m-T-1}{2}\right\rfloor. \tag{33}
\]
If \(T=m\), even \(c=0\) violates the strict inequality.  For the all-active design, \(N_{11}^{k\ell}=m\) and the other three support counts vanish.  Hence \(T=2\) when \(m\ge2\).  In particular, for \(m\ge3\), (33) gives
\[
 c_{\max}=\left\lfloor\frac{m-3}{2}\right\rfloor,
\]
as claimed.

sampling_model.design: There are \(m\) labeled environments; an unknown set \(H\) of size \(h=m-c\) follows one population BACKSHIFT covariance model and the remaining \(c\) slots are arbitrary elements of \(\mathbb S_{++}^{p}\).
sampling_model.units: For population identification only \(\Sigma_e\) is observed. At each index \(n\), every slot supplies an independent within-environment sample of size \(n\) used to construct the indexed simultaneous covariance region \(\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\).
sampling_model.treatment: Unknown additive shift interventions have diagonal covariance \(\operatorname{diag}(s_e)\); intervention targets and strengths are not observed.
sampling_model.overlap: The two candidate honest subsets may overlap in only \(m-2c=h-c\) slots.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance is estimated for the population theorem. Compatibility permits an invariant nuisance in \(\mathbb S_{+}^{p}\); the sharp converse and conditioning analysis impose the explicit interior condition \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{++}^{p}\). The inference layer propagates indexed honest-slot simultaneous covariance regions through feasibility-oracle constraint inversion and measures all perturbations in operator norm.

estimand_functional: For a fixed honest design \(D,H,s\), let robust recovery mean that \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)=\{D\}\) for every positive-definite assignment to the \(c\) slots in \(E\setminus H\). For every \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_+^p\) producing positive-definite honest covariances, \(\delta_H>c\) implies robust recovery. If \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{++}^p\), robust recovery holds if and only if \(\delta_H>c\). Thus \(\delta_H>c\) is minimax sharp over the published positive-semidefinite invariant-noise class, with failure witnessed in its positive-definite subclass.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The population BACKSHIFT solution is unique exactly when every pair of intervention-variance profiles is noncollinear.
An exact non-unitary joint diagonalizer is essentially unique if and only if the diagonal-profile collinearity modulus is below one.
Outlier target matrices are omitted by iteratively retaining matrices whose geometric residual is below a chosen threshold.

Theorem 1 gives noiseless unique topology identification when the exogenous-covariance factor has Kruskal rank at least two, nonzero edges are continuously distributed, and at least two off-diagonal nonzero entries are known in every column.
Simultaneous diagonalizability by congruence of a complete Hermitian family is equivalent to positive-definite feasibility of a linear matrix system.
Pairwise environment comparisons identify causal structure with high probability under probabilistically sparse mechanism changes.
Identification-robust tests and confidence sets maintain uniform asymptotic size across weak and strong identification regimes.

tldr: Unknown shift interventions identify a cyclic linear causal system because covariance differences share a non-unitary congruence diagonalizer. The field-tier kernel asks how many entire covariance environments may instead be arbitrary. The structural matrix satisfying the BACKSHIFT unit-diagonal and cycle-product normalization survives every \(c\)-slot positive-definite replacement if and only if deleting the largest affine-line subset from every pairwise honest shift cloud costs more than \(c\) environments. The converse uses the explicit interior condition on invariant noise to produce a legal positive-definite contamination and a second cycle-product-normalized system. A generic sparse-support formula turns the distance into a combinatorial design criterion; finite subset enumeration is only a reduction to an exact feasibility oracle, while operator-norm contraction of indexed confidence unions, rational certificates, and mandatory abstention at zero affine separation remain the computational agenda for updating the CRAN pooled-difference workflow.

project_justification.gap: Published BACKSHIFT identifies from an entirely honest environment family, general joint-diagonalization theory studies one complete matrix family, and existing outlier-aware joint diagonalization uses a tuning threshold without an exact adversarial radius.
project_justification.niche: Whole-environment replacement creates a discrete overlap geometry: two explanations may discard different slots and therefore share only \(m-2c\) covariance matrices. Affine rather than linear collinearity is the invariant obstruction because the common nondiagonal noise covariance disappears only after differencing.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the necessary-and-sufficient distance \(\delta_H>c\), a matching positive-definite contamination witness satisfying the BACKSHIFT cycle-product normalization under the interior-noise condition, and the exact generic support-incidence formula. Finite subset enumeration is recorded only as a definitional feasibility-oracle implementation note. The open inference target asks for explicit operator-norm radius and modulus functions for indexed confidence unions on fixed-margin uniform classes, rational certificates, chart switching, and abstention at vanishing affine minors.

related_work: The field-tier radius result is informed by RothenhauslerEtAl2015BackShift, Theorem 1 and its appendix proof, which supplies the all-honest model, pairwise profile reduction, and cycle-product normalization; its generic-amplitude result is Corollary 2(ii). KleinsteuberShen2013NUJDUniqueness, Theorem 1, informs the complete-family uniqueness step through profile collinearity. AkhavanEtAl2019GeometryJD, Section 4.2 and equation (42), informs the robust joint-diagonalization setting by trimming outlier target matrices with a chosen residual threshold, but it does not state a worst-case replacement radius. ShenEtAl2020RJDSEM, Section III.C and equations (27)--(28), defines R-JDSEM through an elementwise \(\ell_1\) joint-diagonalization loss for sparse node- or entry-level outlier components within local covariance matrices, rather than replacement of whole covariance slabs. Its noiseless anchored or known-edge Theorem 1 establishes a sufficient uniqueness result under prior edge information; it gives neither an adversarial whole-environment replacement radius, the criterion \(\delta_H>c\), nor a legal two-explanation BACKSHIFT converse. PerryVonKugelgenScholkopf2022SparseShift, Corollary 4.2, Theorem 5.3, and Corollary 5.4, shows how pairwise environment comparisons and sparse mechanism changes support detection and graph recovery, while PfisterPeters2022SparseIV, Theorem 3, illustrates how a support pattern can control generic causal identifiability. LeNguyen2022HermitianSDC, Theorem 7 and Algorithm 5, supplies a complete-family congruence-feasibility primitive; this proposal uses it only to motivate an oracle reduction and does not claim a terminating exact solver. Afsari2008JDSensitivity relates local joint-diagonalization error to conditioning and a uniqueness modulus. AndrewsCheng2013SporadicID motivates confidence procedures that remain valid as identification disappears. None of these sources characterizes adversarial positive-definite replacement of covariance environments under BACKSHIFT normalization and nonnegative raw shifts.
technical_internal_limitation: The exact \(p=2,c=1,m=3\) ambiguity check uses \(D=I_2\), \(D'=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&1/2\\1/2&1\end{psmallmatrix}\), \(\Sigma_1=I_2\), \(\Sigma_2=\operatorname{diag}(2,3)\), and \(\Sigma_3=I_2+D'^{-1}D'^{-\mathsf T}\). Both explanations fit two slots, \(\operatorname{CP}(I_2-D')=1/4\), and \(\Sigma_3\) has positive principal minors \(29/9\) and \(65/9\). This diagnostic is not itself a contribution and does not establish the general converse.
honest_scope: The exact population radius and generic sparse-support frontier are theorem targets. The invariant nuisance is positive semidefinite in the standard BACKSHIFT layer and is required to be positive definite only for the sharp converse, the raw-covariance \(c=0\) reduction, and conditioning claims. Finite subset enumeration is a definitional reduction to a full-solution feasibility oracle, not an encoded solver. The rational certificate atlas, implementable feasibility routine, normalization-chart switching, and operator-norm contraction of \(\mathcal U^{(n)}_{\alpha}\) remain the first-class open question. Contraction is requested only along indexed region sequences with \(r_{n,\alpha,H}\to0\), uniformly on classes bounded away from zero affine separation, normalization slack, and positive-definiteness margins and bounded above in condition number and scale; at \(\gamma_H=0\), set-valued output or abstention remains mandatory. At \(c=0\), the positive-definite raw-covariance criterion is explicitly a non-novel reduction to the published BACKSHIFT noncollinearity result; no statistical rate is claimed without explicit covariance-region inputs.
